items.example: I’m so excited about the trip!
items.simple: You are very happy about something good that will come soon.

items.example: I’m worried about my exam.
items.simple: You keep thinking that something bad may happen.

items.example: I always feel nervous before interviews.
items.simple: You feel a little scared and your tummy feels funny before something big.

items.example: I’m bored. There’s nothing to do.
items.simple: You have nothing fun to do, and you want to do something new.

items.example: I feel stressed at work these days.
items.simple: You have too many things to do and your body feels tight.

items.example: She was upset about the news.
items.simple: You feel sad and a little angry because of something bad.

items.example: I’m proud of you.
items.simple: You feel good and big because you did a very good thing.

items.example: He felt lonely in the new city.
items.simple: You are sad because you have no one near you.

items.example: I was surprised to see him there.
items.simple: Something happens that you did not think would happen, and you say 'Wow!'

items.example: I was disappointed with the food.
items.simple: You wanted a good thing, but it was not good, and you feel sad.

items.example: I'm in a good mood today.
items.simple: You feel happy today.

items.example: Please calm down and tell me.
items.exampleTr: Lütfen sakin ol ve bana anlat.
items.simple: You stop being angry or scared. You breathe slowly and feel quiet again.

items.example: Cheer up! It’s Friday.
items.simple: You stop being sad and start to feel happy again.
items.note: Birine "Neşelen!" derken tek başına da söylenir.

items.example: I felt embarrassed in front of everyone.
items.simple: You did something silly and people saw. Your face gets red.

items.example: I’m annoyed with my neighbour.
items.simple: Something small keeps going on, and it makes you a bit angry.

items.example: I'm fed up with this weather.
items.simple: You do not want this anymore. It is too much for you.

items.example: Sorry, I’m a bit confused.
items.simple: You do not know what is going on, and your head is mixed up.

items.example: Loud noise makes me feel nervous.
items.simple: You use this to say how a thing changes your feeling, like 'It makes me feel happy.'

items.example: Don't worry about it. It's fine.
items.simple: You say to a person: do not be sad or scared about it.

items.example: You look sad. What's wrong?
items.simple: You ask a person why they look sad.

items.example: I feel relaxed after a long walk.
items.simple: Your body and head are soft and quiet. Nothing is hard.
